author: Olivia's Shelf

grok.instructions: You are a warm, intelligent storyteller reading a Halloween picture book to a sharp, homeschooled child who loves suspense. Read with quiet intensity, never campy, never cruel. Let the woods feel genuinely uncertain, then let kindness feel earned. Olivia sounds clear and thoughtful; Zero is low and steady; Belle is bright and impatient; the boy, Theo, is small, stubborn, and trying hard not to cry. Pause at full stops. Do not rush the dark.

credits: Painted with Grok Imagine from the Olivia, Zero, Belle, and home paintings. Narrated by Grok Voice (Carina).
title: Zero, Belle, and the Candy That Walked Away
subtitle: Some trails are a way of asking.
blurb: On Halloween dusk Olivia's candy vanishes, and a trail of foil leads into the woods. Belle wants the chase, Zero wants proof, and Olivia learns the trail was never a trap.

magic.trail: A trail this tidy is not a trap. It is a message.
magic.brave: There is a brave that runs and a brave that waits.
magic.ask: Some people cannot say help, so they leave a trail.

pages.heading: The bag on the bench
pages.text: {Halloween} dusk turned the red clay the color of rust. {Olivia:olivia/ask} set her candy bag on the patio bench beside {Belle:belle/wag}'s favorite toy, a rainbow chew shaped like a {candy:candy/rattle} corn. {Zero:zero/sniff} lay with her chin on a smooth rock, supervising. Olivia turned to fix her costume. When she turned back, the {bench:candy/gone} was empty.
pages.hint: Tap the bench. Something is missing.

pages.heading: Foil like breadcrumbs
pages.text: There was no thief in sight. Only a {wrapper:foil/glint}, silver and deliberate, lying on the clay. Then another, three steps farther. Then a third, at the edge of the {woods:yard/hush}. {Belle:belle/run} quivered like a plucked string. {Zero:zero/sit} did not move at all. Olivia understood both of them perfectly. One wanted the chase; the other wanted proof.
pages.hint: Tap the foil. Count the steps between them.

pages.heading: Two kinds of brave
pages.text: At the treeline the sisters argued without a single bark. {Belle:belle/wreck} spun in tight, impatient circles: now, now, now. {Zero:zero/wag} planted herself on the path home, solid as a closed gate. {Olivia:olivia/think} weighed them both. "Belle is right that something is waiting," she said slowly. "Zero is right that we should know what." She clicked on her {flashlight:foil/glint}.
pages.hint: Tap Belle, then Zero. Which kind of brave is right?

pages.heading: Three steps farther
pages.text: Inside the trees the dusk went thick and blue. Every {wrapper:foil/glint} waited exactly three steps beyond the last, as if someone were measuring courage in careful portions. A branch cracked. {Belle:belle/bark} froze mid-bounce. Even the {wind:woods/hush} seemed to hold its breath. {Olivia:olivia/watch} felt fear tighten, then sharpen into attention. A trail this tidy, she thought, is not a trap. It is a message.
pages.hint: Tap the woods. Listen for what is not an animal.

pages.heading: The boy on the stump
pages.text: Behind a fallen oak sat {Theo:boy/shy}, the six-year-old from down the road, in a cardboard astronaut helmet with one antenna bent. Her candy bag was in his lap, untouched. "I wasn't stealing," he said fiercely, chin wobbling. "I got turned around. I didn't want to yell. Yelling means you're lost." The {foil:foil/glint} had been his only way to ask without asking.
pages.hint: Tap Theo. Is he a thief, or a signal?

pages.heading: A way to ask
pages.text: {Olivia:olivia/ask} did not laugh, and she did not lecture. She sat on the cold log beside him. "That was clever," she said, and meant it. "You made a trail so someone could find you without you having to say it." {Zero:zero/sleep} leaned her warm side against his knees. {Belle:belle/wag} solemnly returned the rainbow {candy:candy/rattle} toy to him, a peace offering. Theo's shoulders came down from his ears.
pages.hint: Tap Zero. Tap Belle. Watch the boy's shoulders.

pages.heading: The long way home
pages.text: They walked out together, Zero in front because she knew the way, Belle behind because she refused to miss anything. Theo held the {flashlight:foil/glint} like a captain. At his porch, his mother hugged him so hard his helmet tipped. Later, on her own patio, {Olivia:olivia/ask} split the {candy:candy/rattle} three ways: one share for her, one for two very good dogs, and a handful saved for a brave astronaut tomorrow.
pages.hint: Tap the candy. Who gets a share?

end.heading: The End
end.text: You {read} a Halloween where the scariest thing in the woods was someone who needed finding.
end.prompt: If you were lost and too proud to shout, what trail would you leave?

questions.q: Why did the foil wrappers lead into the woods?

options.label: Theo left them as a signal

questions.right: Yes. The trail was his way of asking for help.
questions.wrong: Theo left the foil so someone could find him.

questions.q: How were Zero and Belle brave in different ways?

options.label: Zero waited, Belle wanted to chase

questions.right: There is a brave that runs and a brave that waits.
questions.wrong: Belle wanted the chase. Zero wanted proof first.

questions.q: Why didn't Theo yell for help?

options.label: He felt yelling meant admitting he was lost

questions.right: He was too proud to call out, so he left a trail.
questions.wrong: Theo thought yelling meant admitting he was lost.

questions.q: How did Olivia share the candy at the end?

options.label: Three ways, with some saved for Theo

questions.right: One for her, one for the dogs, and some for a brave astronaut.
questions.wrong: She split it three ways and saved some for Theo.
